main_body: A flat green ground patch (grass) with a repeating tuft pattern, laid 4x3 tiles; no standing object.
top_band: none (flat ground tile pattern; the column scan shows only a repeating dark/mid green rhythm, no top surface or front face)
evidence: Terrain ground tiles, not a standing object, so the 3/4 top-and-front contract does not apply. The drawing is a flat top-down ground texture with no vertical faces or receding sides. It is a plain repeating grass patch and is correctly labelled terrain, so it passes Part A.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 6 distinct colours and a median of 6 colours per tile, against 80 distinct colours and 26 per tile for the Beodeul grass reference. Its main grass ramp has about 3 steps (deep, mid, one light tuft tone), where the reference uses 5 or more. The tuft motif is stamped identically on a regular grid, so it reads as a mechanical wallpaper repeat rather than hand-shaded grass. There are no large flat fills (0% coverage), the dark pixels are tinted green, and the sparse orange dots are isolated markers. Overall it is clearly thinner than the grass reference.
